• That would result in the need to '**pull yourself together**'.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Sometimes a person's intelligence is not fully appreciated _______ he/she gets an opportunity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - unless.

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Until is used in the context of time and roughly means before and up to the time.
 
• Unless is used in the context of a precondition and means if this condition is not met.
 
• For example:
 
 
• You can't get a job until you have experience*. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• You can't get a job unless you have experience*.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
 
 
• As per the context of the given sentence, **a person's intelligence would be appreciated only under a certain condition.**
 
• Hence, in the blank part of the given question, 'unless' will be the correct choice.**
 

Correct Sentence__:* **Sometimes a person's intelligence is not fully appreciated unless **he/she gets an opportunity.*​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** ​

 
• The clause followed by unless/until is always positive as unless and until are negative conjunctions.
 
• Example:
 
 
• ​*I shall not go to the party unless they don't invite me. (incorrect)*
 
• *I shall not go to the party unless they invite me. (correct)*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Passengers __are requested to go for__ a security check before they proceed to board the flight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - **No improvement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The simple present tense is used when an action is happening right now, to state or ask about things in general, or when it happens regularly or unceasingly.
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• Subject + V1 + object. (Active Voice)
 
• Object + is/am/are + V3 + subject. (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• The verb will take 's/es' in the **active voice** if the given noun/pronoun (3rd person) is singular.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​He plays badminton daily. (active voice)*
 
• *Badminton **is played **by him daily. (passive voice)*
 
 
 
• As per the rule and example given above,** 'are requested to go' **will be used in the **underlined **part.

Correct Sentence__: *Passengers **are requested to go** for a security check before they proceed to board the flight.*

* *​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• Certain verbs used only in the simple present tense are given below:

 
 
• ​See, think, know, possess, like, want, desire, hate, seem, imagine, etc.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​My brother is owning a car. (incorrect)*
 
• *​My brother owns a car. (correct)*

questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Taking the help of people with rich experience of life will saves you much time and effort.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - **will saves you.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The simple future is a verb tense that’s used to talk about things that haven’t happened yet.
 
• Its structure is: 
 
 
• Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Object + shall/will + be + V3 + subject. (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Garg will visit the Taj soon. (Active Voice)*
 
• *The Taj will be visited by Garg soon. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• Hence, in the given part, simple future tense i.e., will save (active form) will be the correct choice.

 

Correct sentence__- *Taking the help of people with rich experience of life will **save **you much time and effort.*

* *​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• There is another way to show that something will happen in the future. It follows the formula:
 
 
• [am/is/are] + going to + [V1].
 
 
 
• ​Example:
 
 
• *​My brother is going to learn** a new language.*
